learn.title: Visiting every node
learn.body: A traversal visits every node once. For a tree there are several orders, and they differ in when the node itself is handled compared with its two subtrees. All three are short recursive functions.

learn.title: In-order
learn.body: Left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree. On a BST this prints values in sorted order.

learn.title: Pre-order and post-order
learn.body: Pre-order prints the node first, then left, then right. Post-order prints left, then right, then the node. Only the position of the `printf` changes. For the tree used here, pre-order gives 5 3 1 4 8 7 9 and post-order gives 1 4 3 7 9 8 5.

learn.title: Free uses post-order
learn.body: A node can be freed only after its children, or the pointers to them would be lost.

learn.title: In-order on 5, 3, 8
learn.body: Tree: root 5, left child 3, right child 8.
steps: Visit 5's left subtree first: it prints 3

questions.prompt: Which traversal prints a BST in sorted order?
questions.explanation: Left is smaller, then the node, then right is larger, at every node.

questions.prompt: In post-order, when is the node itself handled?
questions.explanation: The name tells the position: post means after.

questions.prompt: Tree: root 5, left child 3, right child 8. What is the first value printed by pre-order?
questions.explanation: Pre-order handles the node before its subtrees, so the root comes first.

questions.prompt: Why does `free_tree` free the node last?
choices: Its children are reached through it
questions.explanation: Freeing it first would lose the pointers needed to free the children.

questions.prompt: A traversal visits every node exactly \_\_.
questions.explanation: Each node is handled one time.

questions.prompt: Match each order to its output on the tree 5, 3, 8.
questions.explanation: Only the position of the node among its subtrees changes.

questions.prompt: Order the actions of in-order for one node.
